## Abstract
This report compiles expression studies of Escherichia coli related to heat-shock from the NCBI GEO database. Using the GEO search API limited to "Series" data type (GSE), a total of 50 expression series were found, of which metadata for the top 20 were retrieved. These studies cover various platforms and include both high throughput sequencing and array-based profiling. The studies include accession identifiers, sample counts, brief descriptions, publication dates, and links to FTP directories for downloading data. This compilation provides a useful resource for researchers interested in E. coli heat-shock response transcriptomics, facilitating access to these datasets for further analysis.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** Escherichia coli is a widely studied bacterial model organism, particularly for stress response mechanisms like heat shock, which triggers protective gene expression changes to survive elevated temperatures. Understanding heat-shock expression profiles helps elucidate cellular adaptation and protein homeostasis mechanisms.

**Literature Review.** The datasets retrieved cover recent research from 2020 to 2026 encompassing studies with varied focus on chaperone machinery, ribosomal dynamics, transcriptional regulation, and evolutionary adaptation under heat shock. Key PubMed IDs linked to some datasets include 38979229, 41092901, and 40360840, among others, describing mechanistic insights into E. coli's heat shock pathways.

**Knowledge Gap.** While many individual studies exist, a consolidated list of E. coli heat-shock expression studies with standardized metadata was previously unavailable in a readily searchable format.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** This work aims to provide a comprehensive listing of expression studies for E. coli under heat shock to support meta-analyses and comparative studies, under the hypothesis that relevant datasets are present and accessible via GEO.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** A database search was conducted on NCBI GEO for expression studies involving "Escherichia coli" and "heat-shock."

**Materials.** The NCBI GEO database was queried via the GEO search API.

**Procedures.** The query was: organism = "Escherichia coli," term = "heat-shock," entry_type set to "gse" for Series, with a maximum of 20 results returned. Results include accession numbers, sample counts, study titles, summaries, dates, and download URLs.

**Statistical Analysis.** The total count of matching studies was 50; details for the first 20 were retrieved and tabulated.

## III. Results
Table 1 summarizes the first 20 heat-shock related expression studies in E. coli from GEO.

| Accession | Sample Count | Title | Date Public | Experiment Type | FTP Directory URL |
|-----------|--------------|-------|-------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| GSE330026 | 15 | The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock | 2026-05-06 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE330026](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE330nnn/GSE330026/) |
| GSE269907 | 12 | Cellular function of the GndA small open reading frame-encoded polypeptide during heat shock | 2026-02-09 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE269907](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE269nnn/GSE269907/) |
| GSE305556 | 12 | Mechanisms of assembly and function of the Hsp70-Hsp40 chaperone machinery | 2025-10-15 | Other | [GSE305556](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305556/) |
| GSE305476 | 74 | Deciphering Host Stress Responses for Predictable Heterologous Gene Expression in E. coli | 2025-08-21 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE305476](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305476/) |
| GSE283264 | 25 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RNA-Seq) | 2025-06-24 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE283264](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/) |
| GSE272161 | 64 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome | 2025-06-24 | Other; Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE272161](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/) |
| GSE272160 | 4 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RedC) | 2025-06-24 | Other | [GSE272160](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272160/) |
| GSE272159 | 33 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (MicroC) | 2025-06-24 | Other | [GSE272159](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272159/) |
| GSE272158 | 2 | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (HiC) | 2025-06-24 | Other | [GSE272158](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272158/) |
| GSE289056 | 4 | Thermally adapted Escherichia coli keeps transcriptomic response during temperature upshift exposure | 2025-05-29 | Expression profiling by array | [GSE289056](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE289nnn/GSE289056/) |
| GSE195509 | 36 | Characterization of a transcriptional factor FevR, involved in improving folding in the periplasm of Escherichia coli. | 2024-12-31 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE195509](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE195nnn/GSE195509/) |
| GSE233555 | 114 | Calibrated ribosome profiling assesses the dynamics of ribosomal flux on transcripts | 2024-07-10 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing; Other | [GSE233555](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE233nnn/GSE233555/) |
| GSE216100 | 4 | Structure of Escherichia coli heat shock protein Hsp15 in complex with ribosomal 50S sununits bearing peptidyl-tRNA | 2022-11-15 | Non-coding RNA profiling by array | [GSE216100](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE216nnn/GSE216100/) |
| GSE200758 | 12 | RNA sequencing unveils very small RNAs with potential regulatory functions in bacteria | 2022-04-16 | Non-coding RNA profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE200758](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE200nnn/GSE200758/) |
| GSE189206 | 50 | Genome-wide promoter assembly mechanisms in E. coli measured at single base resolution | 2022-02-21 | Genome binding/occupancy profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE189206](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE189nnn/GSE189206/) |
| GSE173614 | 18 | Virus-Host interaction of E. coli DksA-deficient cells infected by phage P1vir | 2021-04-30 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE173614](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE173nnn/GSE173614/) |
| GSE144943 | 23 | AzG facilitated RNA dynamic analysis in E.coli | 2020-11-01 | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | [GSE144943](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE144nnn/GSE144943/) |

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The retrieved data demonstrate a range of heat-shock response studies in E. coli span the last few years, including both RNA expression and broader genomic architecture analyses.

**Context.** The listing aligns with the literature documenting molecular components involved in heat-shock response such as chaperones and transcription regulators, and it provides direct pathways to data downloads.

**Limitations.** Only 20 of 50 total hits were retrieved in detail due to query limits. Expression value matrices require separate downloads and processing. The studies vary in experimental design and platform, so comparative analysis requires normalization.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** This catalog enables molecular microbiology and bioinformatics researchers to efficiently locate E. coli heat-shock expression datasets across various platforms and study types. Further work may extend to retrieving all 50 fully and integrating expression data for meta-analyses.

## References
[1] NCBI GEO Search, Escherichia coli heat-shock studies, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE330026 and others as listed above.

## Acknowledgments
National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for GEO data access and resources.
